goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, already adding about 4% to Liverpool for United's leaky defence (16 conceded in six) and taking Sesko off United. Liverpool's attack is close to full strength apart from Ekitiké (counted), while Shaw's injury weakens United's left side; that roughly balances a likely cautious mid-block in Pochettino's first game, so I stay at 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners. With Frimpong available again for Liverpool's right flank and United expected to sit deeper and break under their new manager, Liverpool should spend long spells pushing wide, so I lean mildly higher: about 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already adding about 39% for the derby, a little for Sam Barrott (4.1 a game) and for United's high recent card count (16 in six). A counter-attacking United may give away tactical fouls, but the derby boost is already large, so I stay at 6.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, already adding about 12% to United for their busy attacking under Carrick (96 shots in six). In Pochettino's first game, away at Anfield and set up to counter, United are likely to shoot less than that, which partly offsets Liverpool's near-full attack: about 30.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. United taking fewer attempts in a cautious first game under Pochettino pulls one way, while Liverpool's forwards, with Wirtz in good form, are mostly fit, which pulls the other, so I stay at 9.8.

analyst_view.overall: Liverpool (4th, 18 points) host Manchester United (18th, one league win all season) in the derby, and it is Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge after Michael Carrick's sacking; he only started on 18 November and is expected to keep Carrick's 4-2-3-1 with a mid-block rather than risk a high press. Liverpool under Andoni Iraola have won only one of five home league games but are dangerous on the break; van Dijk has trained, Gravenberch is managing heel pain and Frimpong is back in training, while Ekitiké, Bradley and Leoni are out. United are without Sesko, Baleba and Ugarte (counted) and Luke Shaw is injured, leaving Amass or Dorgu at left-back, while Lisandro Martínez is back from a ban and Maguire recovered from a back spasm. The derby boost to cards (about +39%) and referee Sam Barrott (4.1 cards a game) are already in the numbers.
